works.title: Mona Lisa
works.hook: Probably Lisa Gherardini, a Florentine merchant's wife. Leonardo kept working on it for years and never handed it over.

works.title: The Last Supper
works.hook: Painted on a dry wall, not wet plaster, so it began flaking within decades.

works.title: The Birth of Venus
works.hook: One of the first large paintings of a pagan myth since antiquity, rather than a religious scene.

works.title: Primavera
works.hook: Botanists have identified around 500 plants in it.

works.title: The Creation of Adam
works.hook: Part of the Sistine Chapel ceiling, painted 1508–12. The almost-touching fingers are among the most copied images in art.

works.title: The School of Athens
works.hook: Plato and Aristotle stand at the centre. Plato is often said to have Leonardo's face.

works.title: Venus of Urbino
works.hook: Venetian painting was about colour; Florence prized drawing. Titian is Venice's star.

works.title: The Ambassadors
works.hook: The smear across the floor is a stretched skull. Look at it from the side and it snaps into shape.

works.title: The Hunters in the Snow
works.hook: One of a series on the seasons of the year. Peasant life, painted with real affection.

works.title: The Garden of Earthly Delights
works.hook: Paradise on the left, a strange garden of pleasure in the middle, hell on the right.

works.title: The Arnolfini Portrait
works.hook: The mirror reflects two more figures in the doorway. Above it he wrote 'Jan van Eyck was here 1434'.

works.title: Portrait of a Man (Self Portrait?)
works.hook: The original frame reads 'Als ich can', his motto. Many think it's van Eyck himself.

works.title: Léal Souvenir
works.hook: The carved stone parapet is painted so well it looks chipped and real.

works.title: The Ghent Altarpiece
works.hook: Begun with his brother Hubert. It's one of the most stolen artworks in history.

works.title: The Night Watch
works.hook: Actually a daytime scene. Darkened varnish gave it the nickname.

works.title: Self-Portrait with Two Circles
works.hook: Free to see at Kenwood on Hampstead Heath. Nobody agrees what the circles mean.

works.title: Girl with a Pearl Earring
works.hook: Not a portrait but a 'tronie': a study of a character or expression.

works.title: The Milkmaid
works.hook: Quiet everyday life, lit from a window on the left: pure Vermeer.

works.title: Las Meninas
works.hook: The king and queen appear only in the mirror at the back. Velázquez paints himself at the easel.

works.title: The Rokeby Venus
works.hook: A suffragette slashed it with a meat cleaver in 1914. It was repaired.

works.title: The Calling of Saint Matthew
works.hook: A beam of light follows Christ's pointing hand into a gloomy tax office.

works.title: Supper at Emmaus
works.hook: The fruit basket teeters off the table edge, right into your space.

works.title: Judith Slaying Holofernes
works.hook: Artemisia was one of the most successful painters of her day, and among the first women in Florence's Academy.

works.title: The Elevation of the Cross
works.hook: All muscle and diagonal strain: Baroque drama at full volume.

works.title: The Swing
works.hook: A flying shoe, a hidden admirer in the bushes: a flirtatious private commission.

works.title: Pilgrimage to Cythera
works.hook: The French Academy invented a new category for it: the fête galante.

works.title: The Toilet of Venus
works.place: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
works.hook: Painted for Madame de Pompadour, Louis XV's favourite and Boucher's great patron.

works.title: Marriage A-la-Mode: 1, The Marriage Settlement
works.hook: Scene one of six: a money-for-title marriage that ends in disaster.

works.title: Mr and Mrs Andrews
works.hook: Look at Mrs Andrews' lap: it was left unfinished.

works.title: The Blue Boy
works.hook: Sold to an American collector in 1921. Huge crowds came to say goodbye.

works.title: Whistlejacket
works.hook: Life-size, on a blank background. Stubbs knew horse anatomy from dissection.

works.title: An Experiment on a Bird in the Air Pump
works.hook: Science as drama, lit by a single candle. Will the bird survive?

works.title: The Hay Wain
works.hook: It failed to sell in London, then won a gold medal at the Paris Salon of 1824.

works.title: The Fighting Temeraire
works.hook: A Trafalgar warship towed to the breakers by a steam tug. Voted Britain's favourite painting in 2005.

works.title: Rain, Steam and Speed
works.hook: Look closely: a tiny hare runs ahead of the train.

works.title: Wanderer above the Sea of Fog
works.hook: Seen from behind, the figure invites you to stand in his place.

works.title: Liberty Leading the People
works.hook: Painted to mark the July Revolution of 1830. Restored in 2024.

works.title: The Raft of the Medusa
works.hook: Based on a real 1816 shipwreck scandal. Géricault interviewed survivors.

works.title: The Third of May 1808
works.hook: Faceless soldiers, a man with arms flung out like a crucifixion: a model for every anti-war picture after.

works.title: The Nightmare
works.hook: Shown at the Royal Academy in 1782, it caused a sensation.

works.title: The Gleaners
works.hook: Poor women picking up leftover grain, painted with the dignity usually given to heroes. Some critics found it political.

works.title: The Stone Breakers
works.hook: Destroyed in the Second World War. Courbet: 'Show me an angel and I'll paint one.'

works.title: Olympia
works.hook: A modern Paris courtesan in the pose of Titian's Venus. The 1865 Salon was outraged.

works.title: Le Déjeuner sur l'herbe
works.hook: Rejected by the Salon, shown at the 1863 Salon des Refusés.

works.title: Impression, Sunrise
works.hook: The painting that gave the movement its name, the harbour of Le Havre.

works.title: Woman with a Parasol
works.hook: Monet's wife Camille and son Jean, caught in a breezy moment.

works.title: Water Lilies
works.place: Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York
works.hook: Monet painted his Giverny pond around 250 times.

works.title: Bal du moulin de la Galette
works.hook: A Sunday dance in Montmartre, with dappled sunlight through the trees.

works.title: Luncheon of the Boating Party
works.hook: The woman with the dog is Aline Charigot, later Renoir's wife.

works.title: Paris Street; Rainy Day
works.hook: Haussmann's brand-new Paris boulevards. Caillebotte also funded his friends' exhibitions.

works.title: The Cradle
works.hook: Shown at the first Impressionist exhibition in 1874. Morisot showed in all but one of the eight.

works.title: The Child's Bath
works.hook: The high viewpoint and bold patterns come from Japanese prints.

works.title: A Bar at the Folies-Bergère
works.hook: The reflection in the mirror doesn't quite add up. That's the puzzle.

works.title: The Starry Night
works.place: Museum of Modern Art, New York
works.hook: The view from his window at the asylum in Saint-Rémy. The village was largely invented.

works.title: Sunflowers
works.hook: Painted in Arles to decorate Gauguin's room. There are several versions.

works.title: The Potato Eaters
works.hook: His dark early Dutch period, before Paris turned his palette bright.

works.title: Café Terrace at Night
works.hook: A night scene with no black paint: blues, violets and yellows.

works.title: The Card Players
works.hook: One of five versions. Solid, still, built from blocks of colour.

works.title: Mont Sainte-Victoire
works.hook: Cézanne painted this Provence mountain dozens of times.

works.title: A Sunday on La Grande Jatte
works.hook: Two years of work in tiny dots of colour: pointillism.

works.title: Bathers at Asnières
works.hook: Factory chimneys in the distance: workers relaxing by the Seine.

works.title: Where Do We Come From? What Are We? Where Are We Going?
works.hook: Painted in Tahiti and read right to left, from birth to old age.

works.title: At the Moulin Rouge
works.hook: Lautrec painted himself into the background: the short man in the bowler hat.

works.title: The Great Wave off Kanagawa
works.hook: A print, so many museums own one, including the British Museum. Find tiny Mount Fuji.

works.title: Fine Wind, Clear Morning (Red Fuji)
works.hook: From the same series as the Great Wave: Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji.

works.title: Plum Park in Kameido
works.hook: Van Gogh copied this print in oil in 1887.

works.title: Sudden Shower over Shin-Ōhashi Bridge
works.hook: Rain as fine diagonal lines. Van Gogh copied this one too.

works.title: Folding screen with cherry blossom (detail)
works.hook: Rinpa style: bold, decorative nature against gold leaf.

works.title: The Kiss
works.hook: Real gold leaf. The height of Klimt's 'golden period'.

works.title: Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer
works.hook: Sold at Sotheby's New York in November 2025 for $236.4m, a record for modern art at auction.

works.title: Woman with a Hat
works.place: San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
works.hook: Shown at the 1905 Salon d'Automne, where the 'wild beasts' got their name.

works.title: Dance
works.hook: Just three colours: red, green, blue. Commissioned by the Moscow collector Sergei Shchukin.

works.title: The Scream
works.hook: Munch made several versions. He described sensing 'an infinite scream passing through nature'.

works.title: Saturn Devouring His Son
works.hook: One of the 'Black Paintings' Goya painted straight onto the walls of his house.

works.title: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon
works.place: Museum of Modern Art, New York
works.hook: Even Picasso's friends were shocked. It opened the door to Cubism.

works.title: Nude Descending a Staircase, No. 2
works.hook: Mocked at New York's 1913 Armory Show as 'an explosion in a shingle factory'.

works.title: Udnie
works.hook: Inspired by a dancer Picabia saw on a ship to New York.

works.title: Contrast of Forms
works.hook: Léger's chunky cylinders earned the nickname 'Tubism'.

works.title: Composition VII
works.hook: Kandinsky named his biggest works 'Compositions', like a composer.

works.title: Black Square
works.hook: At its first showing it hung high across a corner, where a Russian home places an icon.

works.title: Suprematist Composition: White on White
works.place: Museum of Modern Art, New York

works.title: Broadway Boogie Woogie
works.place: Museum of Modern Art, New York
works.hook: New York's grid of streets and jazz rhythms, after he moved there in 1940.

works.title: Composition II in Red, Blue and Yellow
works.hook: Only black lines, white, and the three primary colours.

works.title: Composition
works.hook: Mondrian in Paris, breaking trees and buildings into a grid on the way to pure abstraction.

works.title: L.H.O.O.Q.
works.hook: A cheap Mona Lisa postcard with a moustache added. The letters make a rude pun in French.

works.title: Interchange
works.hook: Reportedly sold privately in 2015 for about $300m.

works.title: Campbell's Soup Cans
works.place: Museum of Modern Art, New York
works.hook: 32 canvases, one for each flavour then on sale.

works.title: Salvator Mundi
works.hook: $450.3m at Christie's in 2017, still the auction record. Some experts doubt it's by Leonardo.

works.title: The Shipwreck
works.hook: Tiny people against overwhelming nature: the Romantic 'sublime'.

works.title: Ophelia
works.hook: Elizabeth Siddal posed in a bath of water for months. The plants were painted outdoors by a river in Surrey.

works.title: The Lady of Shalott
works.hook: From Tennyson's poem. Waterhouse painted it decades after the Brotherhood, keeping its love of literature and detail.

works.title: Proserpine
works.hook: The model is Jane Morris. The pomegranate means Proserpine must stay in the underworld.

works.title: Beata Beatrix
works.hook: Rossetti's memorial to his wife, Elizabeth Siddal, painted after her death.

works.title: Norham Castle, Sunrise
works.hook: So loose it looks abstract. Turner never exhibited it.

works.title: Snow Storm - Steam-Boat off a Harbour’s Mouth
works.hook: Turner claimed he had himself tied to a ship's mast to experience the storm.

works.title: Flatford Mill
works.hook: Painted near Constable's family mill in Suffolk: 'Constable Country'.

works.title: Newton
works.medium: Colour print, ink and watercolour on paper
works.hook: Blake shows the scientist as a heroic but blinkered figure, measuring the world with dividers.

works.title: The Great Day of His Wrath
works.hook: John Martin's apocalypse paintings drew crowds like blockbuster films.

works.title: The Painter and his Pug
works.hook: Hogarth's self-portrait with his pug, Trump.

works.title: O the Roast Beef of Old England
Haymakers
works.hook: Stubbs is best known for horses; here he turns to farm workers at harvest.

works.title: Poplars on the Epte
works.hook: One of a series: Monet painted the same trees at different times of day.

works.title: Little Dancer Aged Fourteen
works.medium: Painted bronze with muslin and silk on wooden base
works.hook: The only sculpture Degas ever exhibited, first shown in wax in 1881. This bronze was cast after his death, with a real fabric tutu.

works.title: The Gardener Vallier
works.hook: One of Cézanne's last paintings: the figure built from blocks of colour.

works.title: Farms near Auvers
works.hook: Painted in Van Gogh's final weeks at Auvers-sur-Oise, 1890.

works.title: Clarinet and Bottle of Rum on a Mantelpiece
works.hook: Analytic Cubism: objects split into facets in a narrow palette of browns and greys.

works.title: Dynamic Suprematism
works.hook: Malevich's Suprematism: pure geometric shapes, no objects at all.

works.title: Cossacks
works.hook: Riders and lances are still just visible. Kandinsky was on the edge of pure abstraction.

works.title: Composition with Yellow, Blue and Red
works.hook: Black lines and primary colours: the classic De Stijl look.

works.title: Fountain
works.hook: A shop-bought urinal signed 'R. Mutt'. The original was lost; Tate's is a 1964 replica.

works.title: Metamorphosis of Narcissus
works.hook: Dalí showed this to Sigmund Freud in London in 1938.

works.title: Lobster Telephone
works.medium: Steel, plaster, rubber, resin and paper
works.hook: Made for the collector Edward James. Real phone, plaster lobster.

works.title: The Reckless Sleeper
works.hook: Magritte's dream objects: everyday things placed where they don't belong.

works.title: Celebes
works.hook: Ernst built this elephant-like machine from a photo of a corn bin.

works.title: Black on Maroon
works.medium: Oil paint, acrylic paint, glue tempera and pigment on canvas
works.hook: One of the Seagram murals Rothko gave to Tate. They arrived on the day he died in 1970.

works.title: Summertime: Number 9A
works.medium: Oil paint, enamel paint and commercial paint on canvas
works.hook: Pollock dripped and poured paint onto canvas laid on the floor.

works.title: Marilyn Diptych
works.hook: Made in the weeks after Marilyn Monroe's death in 1962. Colour on the left, fading black and white on the right.

works.title: Whaam!
works.medium: Acrylic paint and oil paint on canvas
works.hook: Based on a panel from a 1962 war comic. Note the Ben-Day dots.

works.title: A Bigger Splash
works.hook: Two weeks to paint a splash that lasts two seconds, as Hockney put it.

works.title: Mr and Mrs Clark and Percy
works.hook: Fashion designer Ossie Clark and textile designer Celia Birtwell. Percy is the cat.

works.title: The Resurrection, Cookham
works.hook: The dead rise in Spencer's home village of Cookham, Berkshire.

works.title: Totes Meer (Dead Sea)
works.hook: 'Dead Sea': a graveyard of wrecked German aircraft, painted in WWII.

works.title: Pelagos
works.medium: Elm and strings on oak base
works.hook: Hepworth carved it in St Ives; the strings echo the sea and sky of Cornwall.

works.title: Girl with a White Dog
works.hook: Freud's first wife, Kitty Garman, painted with intense detail.

works.title: Three Studies for Figures at the Base of a Crucifixion
works.hook: Shown in London in April 1945. It caused a sensation.

works.title: Fall
works.hook: Op Art: one black line, repeated, that seems to move.

works.title: The Dance
works.medium: Acrylic paint on paper on canvas

works.title: Pharmacy
works.medium: Glass, faced particleboard, painted MDF, beech, ramin, wooden dowels, aluminium, pharmaceutical packaging, desks, office
works.hook: Hirst also opened a real restaurant called Pharmacy in Notting Hill.

works.title: Studland Beach
works.hook: Painted on a Dorset beach. Bell simplifies figures into flat blocks of colour.

works.title: Bathing
works.hook: Made for a Borough Polytechnic decoration scheme in 1911.
